concepts.name: Packages and main function
concepts.summary: Recall that every Go file belongs to a package and that an executable starts at func main in package main.

concepts.name: Variable declaration forms
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between var declarations and the := short form and when each is allowed.

concepts.name: Basic built-in types
concepts.summary: Recognise Go's basic types and understand that Go does not convert between them implicitly.

concepts.name: Zero values
concepts.summary: Explain that every declared variable has a defined zero value such as 0, empty string, false or nil.

concepts.name: Control flow with for and if
concepts.summary: Understand that for is the only loop keyword and how if and switch work without parentheses.

concepts.name: Functions and multiple returns
concepts.summary: Understand how to declare functions with typed parameters and return several values.

concepts.name: Go command basics
concepts.summary: Recall what go run, go build and gofmt do and use them to compile and format a program.

misconceptions.text: Go converts between numeric types automatically, so adding an int to a float64 just works.
The := operator can be used anywhere, including at package level outside functions.
Go has while and do-while loops in addition to for.

concepts.name: Slices and backing arrays
concepts.summary: Use slices, len, cap and append, understanding that slices reference an underlying array.

concepts.name: Maps
concepts.summary: Create and use maps, check key presence with the comma-ok form, and know nil maps cannot be written to.

concepts.name: Structs and methods
concepts.summary: Define struct types and attach methods to them using value or pointer receivers.

concepts.name: Pointers and value semantics
concepts.summary: Apply & and * and predict when a function receives a copy versus a reference to data.

concepts.name: Error values and returns
concepts.summary: Return and check error values explicitly following the standard if err != nil pattern.

concepts.name: Defer statements
concepts.summary: Use defer to run cleanup such as closing files, knowing it executes in last-in-first-out order at function return.

concepts.name: Modules and imports
concepts.summary: Create a module, import standard and third-party packages and understand exported capitalised names.

concepts.name: Range loops over collections
concepts.summary: Iterate over slices, maps, strings and channels with range and interpret the index and value it yields.

misconceptions.text: Assigning one slice to another copies the underlying data.
A method with a value receiver can modify the original struct.
Go uses exceptions, so errors are caught with try/catch.

concepts.name: Interfaces and implicit satisfaction
concepts.summary: Define small interfaces and use types that satisfy them implicitly without an implements declaration.

concepts.name: Error wrapping and inspection
concepts.summary: Wrap errors with %w and analyse chains using errors.Is and errors.As to decide how to handle failures.

concepts.name: Goroutines
concepts.summary: Start goroutines and reason about their lifetime relative to the main function.

concepts.name: Channels and select
concepts.summary: Communicate between goroutines using buffered and unbuffered channels and select, analysing blocking behaviour.

concepts.name: Synchronisation with sync package
concepts.summary: Use WaitGroup and Mutex to coordinate goroutines and protect shared state.

concepts.name: Table-driven testing
concepts.summary: Write tests with the testing package using table-driven cases and subtests.

concepts.name: Type assertions and switches
concepts.summary: Analyse interface values dynamically using type assertions and type switches.

concepts.name: HTTP servers with net/http
concepts.summary: Build a simple HTTP service using handlers, a mux and JSON encoding.

misconceptions.text: A type must explicitly declare that it implements an interface.
The program waits for all goroutines to finish before main exits.

concepts.name: Context cancellation and deadlines
concepts.summary: Propagate cancellation, deadlines and request-scoped values through call chains and evaluate where they must be honoured.

concepts.name: Concurrency patterns
concepts.summary: Choose between worker pools, pipelines and fan-out/fan-in designs and justify the choice.

concepts.name: Goroutine leaks and races
concepts.summary: Diagnose data races and leaked goroutines using the race detector and reasoning about channel ownership.

concepts.name: Interface design principles
concepts.summary: Evaluate where interfaces belong and how large they should be to keep code decoupled and testable.

concepts.name: Generics and constraints
concepts.summary: Analyse when type parameters and constraints improve code over interfaces or duplication.

concepts.name: Benchmarking and profiling
concepts.summary: Measure performance with benchmarks and pprof and identify bottlenecks before optimising.

concepts.name: Package and project layout
concepts.summary: Evaluate how to structure packages, internal directories and dependencies for maintainable modules.

misconceptions.text: Generics should replace interfaces wherever possible.
A mutex-free program using goroutines is safe if it appears to give the right output in testing.
Adding more goroutines always makes a program faster.

concepts.name: Scheduler and memory model
concepts.summary: Evaluate concurrent code against the Go memory model and the runtime scheduler's behaviour.

concepts.name: Garbage collector tuning
concepts.summary: Assess allocation behaviour and escape analysis to reduce GC pressure and judge when tuning is warranted.

concepts.name: Designing public APIs
concepts.summary: Design exported package APIs and version them with semantic import rules to remain compatible over time.

concepts.name: Concurrency architecture design
concepts.summary: Create service architectures that handle backpressure, graceful shutdown and bounded concurrency.

concepts.name: Unsafe and reflection trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge when reflection or unsafe is justified and the risks they introduce.

concepts.name: Observability and production hardening
concepts.summary: Design logging, metrics, tracing and failure handling so Go services can be operated reliably.

concepts.name: Tooling and code generation
concepts.summary: Create custom linters, generators and build workflows that enforce team conventions.

misconceptions.text: Tuning GC settings is the first step to making a Go service fast.
Using unsafe or reflection is fine for speed gains without measuring.
Graceful shutdown is handled automatically when the process receives a signal.
